sources.title: Benin Context Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Country context and food-security conditions through 2025; report published June 2026
sources.methodology: FEWS NET synthesizes Benin's hazard, livelihood and security context.
sources.limitations: High-level synthesis; conflict details and climate attribution are limited.

sources.title: Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion Project (P175043), Additional Financing Request 2: Project Information Document
sources.temporal_coverage: Context data current to December 2024; appraisal-stage project design in February 2025
sources.methodology: World Bank appraisal for northern Benin social-cohesion financing, context and proposed actions.
sources.limitations: Context is not outcome evaluation; measures are proposals.

sources.title: SHARP+ resilience assessment in Benin
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.temporal_coverage: Household survey fieldwork in December 2024; factsheet year 2025
sources.methodology: FAO publisher summary describes a SHARP+ household resilience assessment of 1,076 smallholder farming households across five Ouémé Basin communes using 22 modules.
sources.limitations: The publisher summary describes scope and method but not findings; the linked full factsheet was inaccessible and no outcome claims are inferred.

claims.paraphrase: Southern Benin has two rainy seasons and diversified livelihoods; central and northern areas have one rainy season and mixed farming or agropastoralism.
claims.limitations: Zones are described broadly, not at commune scale.

claims.locator: HTML report, Natural Geography and Common Hazards
claims.paraphrase: Northern drought and dry spells reduce crop yields; pastoralists face degraded pasture and dry-season water scarcity.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FEWS NET links pastoral vulnerability with pasture degradation, water scarcity and resource conflict (Common Hazards).

claims.paraphrase: Southern floods along the Ouémé River and low-lying coast damage crops, displace communities and disrupt infrastructure and market access.
claims.limitations: No dated event or affected-population count is given.

claims.locator: HTML report, Executive Summary and Security and Conflict Context
claims.paraphrase: Insecurity in Alibori and Atacora restricts mobility, farm access and markets while driving repeated displacement.
claims.limitations: Conflict is a food-security driver, not a stated climate effect.

claims.locator: HTML report, Security and Conflict Context
claims.paraphrase: Northern farmer-pastoralist conflicts damage crops and livestock and disrupt farming and pastoral mobility.
claims.limitations: Climate is not established as a cause of specific incidents.

claims.paraphrase: World Bank says northern climate shocks, resource scarcity and soil degradation alter transhumance and can intensify farmer-herder and other tensions.
claims.limitations: Appraisal context; no incident-level causal measurement.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It calls climate a threat multiplier affecting routes and resource competition that heighten tensions (PDF p. 4).

claims.paraphrase: Attacks in Matéri and Kérou (Atakora) and Karimama and Banikoara (Alibori) caused school closures and southward movements, pressuring host communities.
claims.limitations: Examples reflect the February 2025 appraisal period.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report links attacks and displacement with economic, social and environmental pressure on hosts (PDF p. 4).

claims.paraphrase: Proposed financing includes climate-screened water and services, livelihood support and participatory planning for refugee and host communities.

FAO reports that its SHARP+ assessment surveyed 1,076 smallholder households across Zogbodomey, Zagnanado, Glazoué, Djougou and Copargo in December 2024, but the accessible summary does not disclose resilience scores.
claims.limitations: This is an assessment-coverage fact only; the underlying findings are unavailable in the accessible page.

access_audit.locator: HTML report, Executive Summary, Natural Geography, Common Hazards and Security Context
access_audit.notes: Opened and read the full report page, including local climate, livelihood and conflict passages.
Opened and inspected the public project information document, including Benin-specific context and proposed community investments.
Page verifies assessment method, survey size and commune coverage, but not the substantive findings.
OpenKnowledge linked report returned HTTP 403; no results or resilience scores were extracted.

search_audit.query: Benin subnational climate vulnerability northern Alibori Atacora drought flood local livelihoods report 2025 2026
search_audit.outcome: Opened FEWS NET's June 2026 context report and identified the FAO SHARP+ assessment scope; the latter's underlying findings were blocked.

search_audit.query: Benin climate stress explicit conflict mediator farmer pastoralist natural resources northern departments public report
search_audit.outcome: The World Bank document explicitly describes climate-related resource scarcity and altered transhumance routes as contributing to northern community tensions; FEWS NET documents localized farmer-pastoralist conflict.

search_audit.query: Benin insecurity armed groups conflict limits climate adaptation mobility land access Atacora Alibori report
search_audit.outcome: World Bank and FEWS NET passages document attacks, displacement and access constraints in northern communes; no source-stated claim that insecurity caused the climate hazard itself was found.

search_audit.query: Benin northern communes resilience capacity climate adaptation water catchments transhumance local institutions report
search_audit.outcome: World Bank appraisal proposes water, climate-screened infrastructure and inclusive local planning; FAO's assessment page confirms survey coverage but its full findings were inaccessible.

gaps: The FAO SHARP+ summary confirms five-commune survey coverage but its full findings were blocked, so no commune-level scores or vulnerability ranking are included.
The World Bank document is multi-country and its project commitments are proposed rather than evaluated.
Recent FEWS NET conflict statistics are not used to infer that climate conditions caused any specific violent incident.
